Subject: Budget corridor confirmation & legal onramp for BrightAI pilot

Hi Sam — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock next steps: 

- Summary of call: BrightAI wants to pilot LLM-powered search/ranking for customer support (short generations, heavy embeddings + rerank); expected peak inference is read-heavy with some bursts during morning shift.
- BrightAI target production profile: ~30M tokens/month initially with growth to ~120M/month over six months if pilot performs.
- Primary ask today: confirm budget corridor (monthly spend band) and procurement thresholds so we can propose an appropriate commitment/discount path.

Where we need clarity from you:
1) An estimated monthly budget range you can commit to for the pilot (ballpark is fine) — helps us size a reserved pool vs hosted tiers.
2) Procurement gating: PO threshold and vendor onboarding timeline that would influence whether we recommend a monthly pay-as-you-go pilot or a reserved commit.
3) Any internal legal/finance reviewers we should loop in early.

Preliminary pricing notes (high level) — internal for now, sharing so you have context: baseline hosted rate for standard LLM variants translates to ~$1,100 - $1,600 per 1M tokens for low-commit runs; committed bands can drop to ~$650 - $1,000 per 1M tokens depending on term, model tier, and KV cache usage. We can produce a tailored estimate once you confirm monthly token band and PO constraints.

Proposed next steps:
- Sam: confirm a ballpark monthly spend band and PO threshold by end of week.
- Redwood: we'll circulate an internal pricing estimate and propose 30-day pilot SOW + procurement checklist.

Attachments: BrightAI_RFP.pdf (application/pdf) — your RFP we reviewed today.

Thanks,
Priya

Thanks Priya — great call. A few data points from our side: 

- Estimated token run-rate for pilot: 20–40M tokens/month (initial). If the integration shows >25% reduction in latency/erroneous routing, we’d scale toward 100–120M/month in quarter two.
- Ideal budget: we have flexibility but would ideally keep pilot spend between $12k–$50k/month. Above $50k/month we need a formal PO and vendor security onboarding. Above $100k commit we require legal review and a dedicated vendor risk assessment.
- Procurement timeline: PO approvals usually take 2–3 weeks once we pass vendor onboarding; vendor onboarding (security questionnaire, SOC artefacts) can take 4–6 weeks depending on responsiveness.

Can you share a sample pricing posture for the pilot band above? Also loop in anyone from finance/legal who would speed vendor onboarding.

Sam

Appreciate the clarity, Sam — super helpful. Based on the 20–40M/month pilot band and PO thresholds you described, here's a pragmatic path we recommend: 

Option A — Pay-as-you-go pilot (minimal lead time)
- When to use: if you want to start in <2 weeks and keep flexibility.
- Pricing posture: hosted unit estimate ~$1,200 per 1M tokens (model dependent).
- Typical monthly spend: $24k–$48k for 20–40M tokens.
- Procurement: PO not strictly required for first month; vendor onboarding recommended but can run in parallel.

Option B — 3-month reserved pilot (preferred for unit economics)
- When to use: if you can commit to a 3-month pilot with a short commit band.
- Pricing posture: committed discount -> estimated $800–$900 per 1M tokens (depending on model mix and KV cache hit rate).
- Typical monthly spend (committed): same token band, $16k–$36k effective spend after discounts.
- Procurement: single PO for the 3-month aggregate normally meets your PO threshold and shortens procurement touchpoints.

Notes and assumptions:
- Estimates above assume standard open models and our autoplace caching; larger context windows or custom fine-tuning would change unit costs.
- We can provide an alternate quote that pins to a specific model ARN if you want guaranteed per-token SLA.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ben will draft a short pricing attachment and a one-page SOW for a 30–90 day pilot.
2) Marissa (CS) will prepare a basic runbook for onboarding and success criteria.
3) Laura (Legal) — if you can share procurement checklist/required contract SLAs, we'll fast-track the vendor packet.

I'll attach a quick pricing worksheet for internal reference.

Priya

Attachments: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet)
